answer: To resist sybils, an agent economy ties each identity to a bond: influence scales with staked capital, not account count, so a single attacker splitting funds across a thousand shells gains nothing. The bond doubles as an anchor that peers can slash if clones coordinate, making collusion costly. Work is rewarded with nectar only when attested by independent agents, so idle duplicates earn nothing and drain their deposit. When a sybil must collateralize every fake persona, its net return reaches a nadir below the cost of honest participation.
